# DOCX fixtures

Real `.docx` files written by producers that are not this library. Our own
`ToDocx` output shares our conventions, so a reader checked only against it
proves only that the two agree (epic `m2fp`).

- **The corpus (`m2fp.4`):** `word2010-*.docx` (Microsoft Word 2010) and
  `lo26.8-*.docx` (LibreOffice 26.8), five shared recipes each plus `m2fp.2`'s
  `word2010-basic.docx`. EVERY corpus file is read by BOTH applications into
  `<name>.word.json` and `<name>.lo.json`; `test/docx-corpus.test.ts` holds
  `readDocx` to what the two agree on and pins where they do not
  (`disagreements.json`). See *The corpus* below.
- **Not corpus:** `wml-oracle.docx` is `m2fp.3`'s oracle — OURS, read by Word.

## word2010-basic.docx

- **Producer:** Microsoft Word 2010, `Word 14.0 build 14.0.7268`, Russian UI
  (Office UI language 1049; the document's default `w:lang` is `ru-RU`),
  driven through COM automation.
- **Command:** `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/gen-docx-word.ps1`
- **Input:** none but the script: a Heading 1 (`Quarterly Report`), a Normal
  paragraph, a two-item default numbered list, a 16x16 PNG generated by
  System.Drawing, and a hyperlink (`the docs`) to `https://example.com`.
- **SHA-256:** `67544B884EF9D50B80091AC5BF523273596900819141214089A172CB7AF63DB8`
- **Not reproducible byte for byte:** Word writes the save time into
  `docProps/core.xml` (`dcterms:created`/`dcterms:modified`,
  `2026-09-29T07:27:00Z` here) and the Windows account name (`user`) as
  `dc:creator`. A rerun yields a different file; the vendored one is the
  reference.
- **License:** the text, picture and structure are ours. The parts Word adds on
  its own (`theme1.xml`, `stylesWithEffects.xml`, the style and font tables)
  are Word's defaults, emitted into every document it saves.

### What it covers (`test/opcread-docx.test.ts`)

The OPC layer on bytes we did not write: relationships out of Id order
(`rId8` first in `document.xml.rels`), a content type answered through a
`Default` (`png`) rather than an `Override`, and the five relationships
`m2fp.3` follows — main document, styles, numbering, image, external hyperlink.

### What it does NOT cover

- `../` or absolute targets, percent-encoded names, case mismatches — Word 2010
  writes none; those are held by `test/opcread.test.ts` alone.
- Any WordprocessingML semantics. Note for `m2fp.3`: a localized Word writes
  LOCALIZED style ids — the style named `heading 1` has `w:styleId="1"`, not
  `Heading1` — so a style must be recognised by its `w:name` or its outline
  level, never its id.

## wml-oracle.docx and wml-oracle.json

- **Producer of the .docx:** THIS repository — `test/helpers/build-wml-oracle.ts`
  through `buildOoxmlPackage`, byte-reproducible. It is deliberately ours: it
  states shapes Word cannot be made to write (two `w:num`s over one abstract
  num, a toggle restated down one `basedOn` chain) so that Word can be asked how
  it READS them.
- **Producer of the .json:** Microsoft Word 2010 (`14.0 build 14.0.7268`, Russian
  UI), opening the .docx read-only through COM and reporting its COMPUTED
  formatting per paragraph (`Range.Text`, `ListFormat.ListString`,
  `OutlineLevel`) and per word (`Font.Bold/.Italic/.Size/.Name/.NameAscii/.Color/
  .Underline/.StrikeThrough`, `HighlightColorIndex`,
  `Font.Shading.BackgroundPatternColor`).
- **Command:** `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/gen-wml-oracle.ps1`
- **SHA-256 (.docx):** `723ea0c8aa40ba65e1076b2ea68b475de7bc1f856c81871caf863f616ed0be80`
- **What it anchors:** `m2fp.3`'s resolution rules — style chains, toggle XOR,
  direct formatting, default size, theme fonts, list counters across
  interruptions, shared abstract nums, start overrides, `numId 0`, style-driven
  numbering, Markup Compatibility selection and content-control transparency —
  against Word rather than against our reading of ECMA-376.
- **What it does not:** layout, tables, images, fields, or anything Word
  renders but does not expose as a property. One Word version, one UI language
  (Russian); a second consumer would arbitrate.
- **Word's answers that corrected the spec:** none. Word CONFIRMED every open
  question: a toggle restated down one `basedOn` chain stays set (nearer wins
  within a chain; XOR applies only ACROSS the paragraph and character layers);
  a bold paragraph style under a bold character style is not bold; the default
  size is 10pt; a second `w:num` over an already-used abstract num CONTINUES it
  (`4.`); `startOverride` restarts at `5.`; a theme font outranks the literal
  beside it; a `Choice` requiring an unknown namespace yields to `Fallback`.
- **Two things Word taught the builder:** Word 2010 REFUSES a theme part
  lacking `a:clrScheme` and `a:fmtScheme` ("the file is corrupted") — a
  font-scheme-only theme is not enough, so the builder writes minimal valid
  ones; and `Font.Name` reports the RESOLVED face for a theme font while
  `Font.NameAscii` reports the `+`-prefixed theme placeholder (`+Заголовки`),
  the opposite of what the plan guessed.

## The corpus (`m2fp.4`)

Two writers build the same recipes; two readers read every file. The
recipes live in `scripts/gen-docx-corpus-word.ps1` and
`scripts/gen-docx-corpus-lo.py`, kept in step text for text — except `notes`
(`v9j3.3.2`), below.

| Topic | Exercises |
|---|---|
| `styles` | Heading 1–3; a custom paragraph style based on Heading 2; a custom bold character style; direct bold, italic, size, font, colour; the toggle case (the bold character style inside a bold paragraph style) |
| `lists` | a three-level bullet list; a `1.`/`a.`/`i.` numbered list; a list interrupted by a paragraph and continued (`3.`); a restarted list |
| `tables` | a repeating header row; a horizontal merge; a vertical merge; a nested table; a shaded cell |
| `media` | an inline 16x16 PNG; an external hyperlink; an internal link to a bookmark |
| `skipped` | header, footer, footnote, endnote, text box, TOC field, comment, a tracked insertion and deletion, a second section in landscape |
| `tabs` (`v9j3.1`) | a left stop with a dot leader; right, centre and decimal stops; a right stop with a middle-dot leader; a paragraph style with two stops, used once with one stop cleared and once as inherited; default stops only. **LibreOffice** has no `clear`: a paragraph's `ParaTabStops` replaces its style's, so the cleared paragraph states the stop it keeps — and its export writes the `clear` |
| `notes` (`v9j3.3.2`) | **Word:** footnotes (one of two paragraphs), a custom mark `*`, an endnote, a footnote in a table cell placed LAST in section 1, and a second section whose footnotes are lowercase roman and restart each section. **LibreOffice:** its footnote numbering is document-wide, so its file states lowercase roman from `iii` for the whole document instead, plus a custom mark and an endnote |

- **Command:** `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/gen-docx-corpus.ps1 -LoProgram <LibreOffice program dir>`
  (both builders, both readers, SHA-256s); `-SkipBuild` re-reads only;
  `-Only <topic>` builds one recipe and still re-reads every file. Then
  `npx tsx scripts/docx-disagreements.ts`.
- **Not reproducible byte for byte:** both writers stamp `docProps/core.xml`
  with the save time. The VENDORED files are the reference.
- **License:** every text, picture and structure is ours; each writer adds only
  its own defaults (theme, style and font tables).

**Two things LibreOffice WRITES differently, which are the producer's semantics

## Ground truth and reader disagreements

Every corpus file has `<name>.word.json` (`scripts/docx-truth-word.ps1`, Word
2010) and `<name>.lo.json` (`scripts/docx-truth-lo.py`, LibreOffice 26.8), both
in the `DocxTruth` schema of `test/helpers/docx-truth.ts`.

- **Accepted, then read:** both readers COUNT tracked changes and then accept
  them in memory, so paragraphs are the final text, as `readDocx` shows it.
- **`styleName` is recorded and never compared:** Word's UI is Russian
  (`Заголовок 1`), LibreOffice's English (`Heading 1`).
- **Normalizations each reader needed, found by reading its output:** Word's
  `Range.Text` writes an inline picture as `/` and enumerates each table row's
  end mark as an empty paragraph (detected by `Information(31)` on a COLLAPSED
  range); LibreOffice's `ListLabelString` is EMPTY for a bullet (the glyph is the
  level's `BulletChar`), its `getString()` appends footnote and endnote labels,
  and a cell's `getString()` stops at a nested table. A cell's text is its
  NON-EMPTY paragraphs joined by a newline, in both readers and in `truthOf`.
- **`disagreements.json`** is written by `scripts/docx-disagreements.ts` and
  asserted EXACTLY by the test.

### Where Word and LibreOffice disagree

- **A URL's trailing slash** (`word2010-basic`): Word reports
  `https://example.com/`, LibreOffice `https://example.com` as written.
- **TOC hyperlinks** (`lo26.8-skipped`): Word reports the TOC entries' internal
  links (`__RefHeading___Toc…` anchors, one with empty text); LibreOffice none.
- **Headers, footers and fields in a two-section document**
  (`word2010-skipped`): Word counts one header and one footer (section 2 is
  LINKED to section 1), LibreOffice two each (a page style per section); Word
  counts three fields (the TOC and its PAGEREFs), LibreOffice one (the index).
- **A section break's paragraph** (`word2010-skipped`): Word lists it as an
  empty paragraph, LibreOffice folds it into the page style, so every later
  paragraph index is shifted.
- **A vertically merged cell** (both `tables` files): Word lists the covered
  cell's empty paragraph, LibreOffice omits covered cells, so later indices
  shift. `readDocx` lists it, as Word does.

Past a disagreement in LENGTH the test compares elements only up to the shorter
reading, since there the other reader is no witness — but `readDocx`'s OWN
length must still fall between the two readers'. Without that bound a
`readDocx` that stopped at a section break or a merged cell passed the very
files that cover those constructs (final review, mutation-checked).

### Notes (`v9j3.3.2`)

Every truth file carries `notes`: per kind, each note's mark and text.

- **Word's mark is DERIVED:** `Footnote.Reference.Text` is the control
  character 0x02 for an auto-numbered note (probed before the reader was
  written). The script computes the number from what Word reports — the
  note's section, that section's `NumberStyle`, `StartingNumber` and
  `NumberingRule` — counting only auto-numbered notes. The FORMATTING of those
  numbers is the script's. A custom mark is the reference's own text.
- **LibreOffice reports its mark directly:** the anchor's string (`1`, `i`),
  or the label when custom.
- **They disagree on the Word file's footnote marks**, and that is LibreOffice
  ignoring Word's per-section restart: it numbers the whole document with the
  last section's lowercase roman (`i`..`iv`) where Word shows `1 2 * 3 i`.
  So the agree-only comparison cannot see the per-section rule, and
  `test/docx-corpus.test.ts` holds that one file's marks to WORD ALONE.
- **They disagree on a custom-mark note's text:** Word writes the mark into the
  note body as an ordinary leading run; LibreOffice reads it as text
  (`* Starred note.`), Word does not. The renderer drops it (`noteLead`), or
  the mark would be drawn twice — a finding of this corpus, held by
  `test/docx-notes.test.ts`.
- **LibreOffice writes a tab** between its own number and the note text; the
  renderer drops it, or every note would report `w:tab`.
- **Not covered:** per-page restart (it depends on pagination this library does
  not share with Word — `test/flow-notes-page-restart.test.ts` alone holds
  it); a list inside a note (LibreOffice's list-style names vary by version, so
  it is held by `test/docx-notes.test.ts`); Word's `chicago` format past four
  notes, where the engine's `symbols` (`* † ‡ § ¶ #`) and Word's (`* † ‡ §`,
  then doubled) part company.
- **The cell note renders (`v9j3.3.3`):** `word2010-notes.docx`'s footnote in
  a table cell is now DRAWN, and `test/table-notes-frontends.test.ts` holds the
  numbers drawn for the whole file to Word's — compared by number, not
  spelling, since the engine applies the last section's lowercase roman to
  every section (reported) where Word spells section 1 in arabic.
- **Mutation-checked:** of 16 mutations across the engine, the reader and
  the mapper, 15 redden. The corpus reddens the custom-mark and lowerRoman
  rules; the per-page restart, its gutter, the restart marker's lookahead and
  a note citing a note are held by hand-built cases alone. The 16th, dropping
  the placement skip of a restart marker, is EQUIVALENT: the marker places as
  an empty element.

### Tab stops (`v9j3.1`)

Every truth paragraph carries `tabs`: the stops in force, each `{ pos, align,
leader }` with `pos` in points from the margin ROUNDED TO A TWIP, so Word's
points and LibreOffice's 1/100 mm compare exactly (a TOC style's 9351 twips is
467.55pt to Word and 467.5142pt through 1/100 mm).

- **Word lists more than the document states.** `Paragraph.TabStops` also
  holds Word's DEFAULT stops (`CustomTab = False`) and a list number's own tab
  (`w:val="num"`, `wdAlignTabList`); the reader drops both. The leader is
  `TabStop.Leader` — a first draft read a property that does not exist and got
  `none` for every stop, which the disagreements showed at once.
- **LibreOffice** reports `ParaTabStops`, with a `DEFAULT`-aligned entry as its
  placeholder for "default stops only", dropped; `FillChar` arrives as a UNO
  `Char` and is read through `.value`.
- **They agree on every stop in all 16 files**, the cleared style stop
  included, and `readDocx` matches them all — the TOC styles' right-aligned dot
  leaders in the two `skipped` files too. The re-read moved no other field of
  any truth file.

### Where readDocx is held to a known gap

None. `readDocx` agrees with both readers at every path they agree on — about
1,100 leaf values over 11 files — with no `src/` change beyond `m2fp.4`'s own
recording of sections, headers, footers, revisions and simple fields. That was
measured, not assumed: breaking a list format, the toggle XOR or the header
records each reddens the corpus test at the expected files.

## spacing-oracle.docx and spacing-oracle.json (`m2fp.5`)

**What it is.** OURS, not Word's: three paragraphs with EXACT 20pt line
spacing, written by `test/helpers/build-spacing-oracle.ts` (byte-reproducible;
the test asserts the vendored file equals the builder's output). Word 2010
(`14.0 build 14.0.7268`) opens a COPY through COM, sweeps P1's space-after and
P2's space-before over seven pairs, and records each paragraph's position.

**Command.** `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/gen-spacing-oracle.ps1`
(not run by `npm test`; it needs Word). SHA-256 of the `.docx`:
`CF86992DDF5C8892FCD6DFBA3BE7A6B2F1E4ED86F83C77B432A7CD5FE24B09B3`.

**What it found.** Word COLLAPSES adjacent paragraph spacing to the LARGER of
space-after and space-before — (12, 18) and (18, 12) both leave an 18pt gap,
(6, 30) a 30pt one — where `m2fp.5`'s design had assumed they add. The DOCX
importer emits `spaceBefore = max(0, before - previousAfter)` because of it.

**The witness, and why.** P3 carries no spacing at the P2/P3 boundary, so its
position is where P2's line really ended. The position Word REPORTS for a
paragraph that has space before (`Range.Information(6)`) is not trustworthy:
it reads `prevEnd + after + before` even where the layout used the max — which
is how the first run of this oracle came to look additive. That value is kept
as `p2reported` so the discrepancy stays visible. Word 2010's PDF export hung
on this machine (twice, even under a timeout guard), so a PDF could not serve
as the witness instead.

**Ceiling.** One Word version, exact line spacing only — it says nothing about
how Word sizes an AUTO line, nor about HTML auto-spacing
(`beforeAutospacing`), nor about spacing at the top of a page.


## table-spacing-oracle.docx and table-spacing-oracle.json (`m2fp.10`)

**What it is.** OURS, not Word's: a paragraph (P1), a one-cell table with no
borders and zero top/bottom cell margins whose one paragraph has an EXACT 20pt
line and no spacing, a paragraph (P2) and a paragraph (P3), all exact 20pt
lines, written by `test/helpers/build-table-spacing-oracle.ts`
(byte-reproducible; the test asserts the vendored file equals the builder's
output with no arguments). Word 2010 (`14.0 build 14.0.7268`) opens a COPY
through COM, sweeps P1's space-after and P2's space-before over six pairs, and
records the positions of P1, the cell's paragraph, P2 and P3.

**Command.** `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/gen-table-spacing-oracle.ps1`
(not run by `npm test`; it needs Word). SHA-256 of the `.docx`:
`94D31A8A7F8D177F6B772F0ED8012F798A6D1A6FDE8D656A752609D29BD82596`.

**What it found.** A table does NOT collapse spacing. The cell moves down by
exactly P1's space-after and P3 by exactly P2's space-before, each independent
of the other: (12, 18), (18, 12) and (24, 6) apply both in full, where two
adjacent PARAGRAPHS would have kept only the larger. The importer already did
this — the m2fp.5 review suspected otherwise — and
`test/table-spacing-oracle.test.ts` now holds `AddDocx` to the same deltas.

**A trap the first run fell into.** Word counts a table row's END-OF-ROW mark
as a paragraph of its own, so `Paragraphs.Item(3)` is that mark and not P2:
the first run set space-before on it and measured nothing. The script finds
paragraphs by their TEXT.

**Ceiling.** One Word version, one single-row borderless table with zero cell
margins, exact line spacing only. Nothing about a table's own spacing
properties, borders, row height rules, or a table at the top of a page.

## tab-oracle.docx and tab-oracle.json (`v9j3.1`)

**What it is.** OURS, not Word's: seven paragraphs set in Courier New 10pt,
one per tab-stop case — a left stop at 2in, a right stop at 4in, a centre stop
at 3in, a decimal stop at 3in before `12.50`, default stops only
(`w:defaultTabStop` 720, two tabs), a style chain whose child clears an
inherited stop, and a dot leader to a right stop at 5in. Each case puts a
unique upper-case MARKER after its tab. Written by
`test/helpers/build-tab-oracle.ts` (byte-reproducible; the test asserts the
vendored file equals the builder's output). Word 2010 (`14.0 build 14.0.7268`)
opens a COPY through COM and records each marker's left edge,
`Range.Information(5)`, in points, with the face it laid the marker out in.

**Command.** `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/gen-tab-oracle.ps1`
(not run by `npm test`; it needs Word). Run 2026-10-08. SHA-256 of the `.docx`:
`7BBB60B05A38FE4130C0DCDA5D63A72D5C98C462E847D0CEFBAA0E19EB2D9B78`; of the
`.json`: `BD924176C29B44BAA5DD76082527003B7484731EDCBCC2E873C8E16840887A12` (LF, as committed; the script writes CRLF).

**What it found.** Nothing to correct: `AddDocx` lands all eight markers
exactly where Word does. Stops are measured from the margin, a stop is chosen
past the pen, a cleared inherited stop is gone, and right, centre and decimal
alignment measure the segment as Word does.

**Why every case is exact.** Word reports `Courier New` for every marker, and
the importer — with no font folder registered — substitutes Courier, whose
600-unit advance is Courier New's. So a right, centre or decimal target is
metric-exact rather than off by a substituted face's width.

**Ceiling.** One Word version, one fixed-pitch face, single-line paragraphs.
Nothing about a stop past the right margin, a tab that wraps, a leader's own
glyph positions (only where the text after it lands), justified tabbed lines,
